clue.text: Opens second page and studies

parts.note: to study a text is to read it, so studies means reads

explanation.surface: Someone opens a book at the second page and settles down to study it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opens' looks like the start of a sequence of actions, but it is the definition, a verb in the third person like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread something, a map or wings say, is to unfold or open it out.

clue.text: Organ pipe player's unfinished line

parts.note: Pan, the Greek god of the wild, is famous for playing the panpipes

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for line loses its final letter

parts.note: a crease is a line folded or pressed into cloth or paper

explanation.surface: An organ pipe player has left a line of music incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ pipe' reads as a church instrument; split it so 'Organ' is the definition and 'pipe player' is the god Pan. 'unfinished' drops the last E of CREASE.
explanation.definitionFit: The pancreas is a gland in the abdomen, one of the body's organs.

clue.text: Shocking vote for right's idealistic — empty

parts.note: to vote for a candidate is to elect them
R is the abbreviation for right

indicators.note: empty means the word idealistic is emptied, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A voter backs a right-wing idealist whose ideas turn out to be hollow and shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric shock is the jolt from current, so shocking can describe something electric, and electric also means thrilling.

clue.text: Put off by explosive? Dazed capital's resolute

indicators.note: by means next to, so the explosive sits beside the word for put off

parts.note: to put someone off is to deter them
a mine is an explosive device

indicators.note: capital means the capital, or first, letter of the word Dazed

explanation.surface: Someone deterred by a blast, left dazed in the capital, is somehow still resolute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' suggests a city, but it means the capital letter of 'Dazed', a D.
explanation.definitionFit: A determined person is firm in purpose, unwilling to give up: resolute is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Villain — current and in the past

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics
ago means at a time in the past

explanation.surface: A villain who is both current and in the past, a lasting menace.
explanation.walkthrough: IAGO is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the treacherous ensign who destroys Othello in Shakespeare's tragedy, a classic stage villain.

clue.text: Whip casserole up after siesta

parts.note: the cat, short for cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for casserole is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel, here standing for a casserole dish

explanation.surface: A cook whips up a casserole after an afternoon nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' and 'up' look like a cooking instruction; the whip is a CAT and 'up' turns PAN into NAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short sleep taken during the day, much like a siesta.

clue.text: Primate of all Ireland's backing progress first

indicators.note: first means the word for progress comes before the rest

parts.note: to go is to proceed or make progress

indicators.note: backing means the words all and Ireland are reversed together

parts.note: taken as written
IR is the abbreviation for Ireland

explanation.surface: The Primate of All Ireland, the senior archbishop, is backing progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate of All Ireland' is a real church title, which is the surface's trap; 'backing' turns ALL plus IR into RILLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla is the largest of the great apes, which belong to the primate order of mammals.

clue.text: Policeman's taking puff? Shock horror!

parts.note: DI stands for Detective Inspector, a police officer; with the 's it gives DIS
a gust is a puff or blast of wind

explanation.surface: A detective takes a drag on a cigarette, to general outrage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link word: the DI's piece simply comes before GUST.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgust is strong revulsion, the feeling a tabloid's mock-outraged 'shock horror!' pretends to express.

clue.text: A Roman in charge cooked his speciality?

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are mixed up as if stirred in a pot

explanation.surface: An Italian chef in charge of a kitchen cooked his signature dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole surface: the Roman's speciality would be a pasta.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaroni is a tube pasta, the kind of dish an Italian cook might be known for.

clue.text: Agreement from different enterprises

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An agreement reached between two different businesses.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly understanding between states, a form of agreement.

clue.text: It's more filling between courses

parts.note: courses here are layers of bricks, and the mortar packed between them is the filling, not food between dinner courses

explanation.surface: Something more filling to eat between the courses of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' and 'filling' suggest a meal; in building, courses are rows of brickwork and 'more filling' is mortar.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointing is the mortar finish pressed into the joints of brickwork, filling the gaps between rows.

clue.text: Finish following, say, minor slip

indicators.note: following means the word for finish comes after the other piece
say signals that the word for minor is spoken, giving a sound not its spelling

parts.note: petty means minor or trivial
a coat of paint or varnish is a finish

explanation.surface: Someone finishes off after a minor slip-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slip' looks like a mistake; it is the undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A petticoat is a woman's underskirt, also called a slip.

clue.text: Credit's hidden charge produces depression

indicators.note: hidden means the word for charge is concealed inside the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: A credit card's concealed fee leaves the borrower depressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' suggests low spirits or a slump; it is a hollow in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow, a depression in the surface of the ground.

clue.text: For example, London underground's endless elegance

parts.note: the metro is an underground railway

indicators.note: endless means the word for elegance loses its last letter

parts.note: polish means refinement or elegance

explanation.surface: The London Underground is said to be endlessly elegant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pins 'London' to 'underground'; it actually goes with 'For example' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: London is a great capital city, an example of a metropolis.

clue.text: Casual and cool as I can, possibly

indicators.note: possibly means the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone tries to act as casual and cool as they can.
explanation.definitionFit: Occasional work is irregular and casual, done now and then rather than steadily.

clue.text: Not entirely spellbinding sorcerers

indicators.note: not entirely means the word for spellbinding is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: magic as an adjective means enchanting or spellbinding

explanation.surface: Sorcerers who are not entirely spellbinding.
explanation.walkthrough: MAGI are also the three wise men of the Nativity.
explanation.definitionFit: Magi were priestly wise men of ancient Persia, reputed to practise sorcery, the root of the word magic.

clue.text: Swayed a month back on rip-off French wine

indicators.note: on means the reversed month is placed after the other pieces in this across entry

parts.note: a con is a swindle or rip-off
vin is French for wine

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for the month is reversed

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: A month ago someone was swayed into buying an overpriced French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: To be convinced is to be persuaded, won over by argument.

clue.text: Order is, "sloped rifles"

indicators.note: order means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant's command: slope arms with rifles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifles' looks like the guns of the drill order; it is a verb meaning plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to ransack it, and to despoil is to strip or plunder.

clue.text: Orientation of bachelor with jewellery's right off!

indicators.note: off means the letter for right is removed from the word for jewellery

parts.note: earrings are items of jewellery

explanation.surface: A bachelor gets his jewellery stolen.
explanation.definitionFit: Your bearings are your sense of where you are and which way you face, your orientation.

clue.text: She's maybe recast by direction

indicators.note: maybe means the letters of recast could be ordered otherwise

parts.note: S, for south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A performer might be recast by the director.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recast' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder; 'maybe' is the signal, giving ACTRES before S.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman performer, so she is a fair cryptic stand-in for one.

clue.text: Cover point has someone relatively close

parts.note: S is a compass point, south
a mother is a close relative

explanation.surface: In cricket, the fielder at cover point has a close relative watching.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover point is a cricket fielding position; split it so 'Cover' is the definition and 'point' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it thickly or completely.

clue.text: When team leaders are sent off, fixture's tied

indicators.note: the leading letters of the word for team are dismissed from it

parts.note: a football or cricket team is an eleven

explanation.surface: With the team captains sent off, the match ends in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team leaders' suggests captains; it is the first two letters of ELEVEN, removed to leave the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tied score is level, with neither side ahead: the score is even.

clue.text: Large Frenchmen after company? Repulsive

indicators.note: after means the Frenchmen come after the company

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation for messieurs, French for gentlemen
odious means hateful or repulsive

explanation.surface: Some large Frenchmen join a company and are found repulsive.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodious means roomy, spacious, so large in capacity.

clue.text: Magic circle's about obsession

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle
C, for circa, means about
a cult is an object of obsessive devotion

explanation.surface: The Magic Circle, the conjurors' society, is all about an obsession.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is a London society of magicians; here 'circle' is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: The occult covers supernatural arts and secret magic.

clue.text: One politician's trickery following recount

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
art can mean cunning or trickery

explanation.surface: A politician's trickery comes after an election recount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recount' looks like a second count of votes; it is a verb meaning tell. 'following' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart news is to tell or relate it, just as to recount a story is to tell it.

clue.text: Resistance to European note — foreign money's withdrawn

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a cent is a coin used in many countries outside Britain

explanation.surface: Resistance to the European currency means foreign money has been withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' looks like money taken out; it describes a reserved person.
explanation.definitionFit: A reticent person is reserved and uncommunicative, the way a withdrawn person keeps to themselves.

clue.text: Nothing or nobody, even initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of the four preceding words are taken

explanation.surface: A definition of nothing or nobody, even at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means not any thing or not any person, so it covers both nothing and nobody.

clue.text: Dicky and I in a state

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or unsound, so the letters are shaky and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky and the speaker are in a state of agitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is a British informal word for faulty, the anagram signal. INDIANA is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Strange new glister but it's not gold!

indicators.note: strange means the letters are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: An echo of the saying that all that glisters is not gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface twists 'All that glisters is not gold'; sterling silver is the precious metal that is not gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterling silver is the standard alloy of silver, a precious metal other than gold.

clue.text: Most oppressive head of state in cabinet

indicators.note: in means the first letter goes inside the word for cabinet

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard or cabinet

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of the word state

explanation.surface: The head of state in the cabinet is the most oppressive of rulers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet' suggests government ministers; it is a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is humid and stifling, so the closest is the most oppressive.
